invariants: Original adoption UUID and completed/validated reversion evidence preserved; new generation has its own immutable UUID/FKs.
Barrier COMMIT atomically requires corporate authority, latches the generation and freezes the historical cutoff.
Dedicated allocation fence avoids locking capture behind the delivery control row.
Old READ COMMITTED writers reject without assignment; old REPEATABLE READ snapshots serialize-fail at the updated fence.
Compatible capture uses durable admissions after the barrier and never calls the local sequence for new calls.
Corporate registry bootstrap preserves all historical non-null IDs; NULL corporate IDs remain unchanged.
Counter lock, registry uniqueness and ALWAYS trigger protect real occupied IDs/reservations under concurrent writers.
Legacy history is registered by bounded batches without renumbering; remote reservation and local checkpoint are separate recoverable transactions.
Remote reserve committed before local persistence and local COMMIT acknowledgement loss recover the same ID/token using original UUIDs.
Quarantines, pending outbox, confirmed receipts, payloads and hashes remain preserved; historical collisions require formal selective isolation.
Protocol queries are local READ ONLY and can inspect uncertain outcomes without remote access.
Source non-owner role can activate with reviewed permissions but cannot disable barriers or reset mandatory authority.
Actual Worker/HttpTransport/Auth/API with loopback synthetic OLOS captures during activation and MADM outage, then materializes and delivers with tokens.

comparison_with_other_worktree.method: Read-only inspection only; no merge, cherry-pick, copy, move or edits.

limitations: Global typecheck still has 17 baseline-identical diagnostics in existing historical integration tests; none suppressed or skipped.
Full integration still has 7 baseline-identical failing history/homologation scenarios plus their parent (8 failed).
DBA approval and real MADM schema/role/TLS/writer compatibility homologation are required; no real installation performed.
No production WAN, OLOS retention, multi-million-row load or production throughput benchmark performed.
After the barrier, rollback to a legacy binary or resetting authority is forbidden; recovery must move forward with the same generation.
Corporate int32 exhaustion or authority outage preserves durable admissions, requiring external capacity/connectivity intervention.
A deliberately privileged DBA can modify/disable database protections; runtime roles must not have that authority.
Historical collisions are not remapped automatically and quarantined rows are not released by readoption.
